scenario: A coordinate-sorted BAM with several reference sequences (e.g. whole-transcriptome or multi-contig) is loaded. parseBAMRecords stops after the first 1000 records of the file, before any per-reference filtering (the caller only filters `r.refID === refIdx` afterwards). If the first 1000 records all map to references other than the loaded gene, zero reads for the gene are ever parsed; checkRefMatch then finds no reads for the gene ref (pick = -1) and falls back to matching the first loaded reference name, so the gene is reported as 'matched' while the Reads view shows nothing. Reads silently dropped / empty view with no explanation.
title: Read cap is applied to the whole file before choosing/parsing the target reference, so a multi-reference BAM can lose every read of the gene

scenario: A BAM from a normal aligned+marked run: reads with flag 0x100 (secondary), 0x800 (supplementary), 0x200 (QC fail) and 0x400 (duplicates) are all kept by parseBAMRecords, and the caller's filter only removes records whose refID differs (no mask on record.flag). Duplicates then double-count every variant base, secondary/supplementary alignments of the same original read appear as independent reads, so base counts and variant fractions in the Reads view ('Sample -> row', codon analysis) are inflated -> wrong genetics. Unmapped reads kept with flag 0x4 and pos -1 also render with refPos -1 ('N' reference everywhere) or zero columns.
title: Secondary, supplementary, QC-fail, duplicate and unmapped reads are parsed and kept with no flag filtering
Same biological indel placed at two CIGAR offsets splits the event key: a deletion carried by all reads stays out of the sample row (false wild type / no frameshift)
scenario: Reference '...AAAAAAAA...'; every read deletes the same 3 As, but the aligner did not left-normalize: half the reads have the 3D starting at 0-based p=10, half at p=11 (a CIGAR nebenform common in homopolymers/repeats; bowtie2/minimap2 do not guarantee one placement). delEv gets keys 10:3 (n=20) and 11:3 (n=20) with depth 40 at positions 10-12, so each frac=0.5: line 95 keeps them, line 96 hom=frac>0.5 is false, line 97 marks nothing deleted, and both are pushed as zyg:'het'. addSampleRowFromReads (script.js:8942) states het indels are not put in the row, so the row shows the full reference with no '-', and Codon analysis / MACSE never see the frameshift. If the event is split 3-ways (frac 0.33) each is still wrongly 'het'; split below 0.2 (line 95) the variants vanish with no message at all. Same mechanism for insertions via the key at line 67.

Load a BAM with e.g. 250,000 records. parseBAMRecords returns { records: 1000, exceededLimit: true, totalReads: 1001 }; the counter is never advanced past MAX_READS + 1, so the returned totalReads is not the number of reads in the file. Any status line / tooltip that uses totalReads tells the user 'N reads' with N = 1001 (or 1000) instead of the real count, while the parser silently dropped the rest of the file.
title: totalReads returned by parseBAMRecords is capped at MAX_READS+1, so a 'reads in file' count shown to the user is wrong
GenBank CDS features are parsed and stored but never wired into the per-gene codon analysis (only BED features are)
scenario: User loads a GenBank file with CDS features (parseGenBank stores them at line 4534 as _genbank: { accession, organism, features }, and a grep of script.js shows that field is set there and never read anywhere else), then turns on Codon analysis expecting the 'per annotated CDS' frame/strand/splice behaviour. _annotCdsFeatures() consults only state._annotPlaced, which is built solely from BED text (parseBedText, line 7742 -> state._annotPlaced at 7849; setAnnotation at ~8050 also calls parseBedText). So no CDS feature is ever taken from the GenBank file: _computeAnnotatedCodonAnalysis returns null, the 'Genes' frame radio stays hidden (13037-13039) and the user silently gets whole-alignment frames instead of the gene-by-gene CDS analysis described in the product flow. I verified the code facts (the one grep for _genbank in script.js returned only the definition line); I could not fully verify the intent, hence confidence 3.

title: _aaByGene merges every unnamed CDS feature into one translation group and applies the first group's strand to all of them
scenario: Load an annotation BED with CDS lines whose name column is '.' or empty (very common in UCSC/IGV tracks), e.g. one CDS on '+' at columns 100-900 and one on '-' at 950-1500, set Codon frame to Genes/Auto. _computeAnnotatedCodonAnalysis pushes each codon entry with gene: d.f.name (undefined, line 5129), so _aaByGene keys both genes under '' (line 5154: key = e.gene || ''), takes the group strand from the FIRST entry (line 5155, the '+' gene) and then applies that single strand to every entry in the group. The '-' -strand gene's codons are joined in alignment-column order (3'-to-5' in its own reading direction) instead of being reversed, so its amino-acid string comes out backwards, and the two unrelated proteins are concatenated into one 'gene' translation row. Any gene-labelled translation row/export per gene is wrong for such files.

title: Frameshift-marked codon box uses a plain space instead of a non-breaking space, so the codon cell collapses
quote: html += `${x.text || ' '}`;
scenario: Codon analysis with a read carrying a non-3-multiple indel: the codon at the run start hits the ${x.text || ' '} fallback with a regular space, unlike the parallel cell at 5314 which uses '\u00A0'. The aa-c span holds only a collapsible space, so the class/stop-coloured codon box loses content/background and the translation row misaligns with the sequence row above.

title: Auto mode latches onto an annotation with 0 usable CDS and never falls back to frame analysis (codon mode goes blank)
scenario: Load a nucleotide alignment plus an annotation track whose CDS features all fail per-gene analysis - e.g. any sequence row contains a character outside IUPAC (an 'X') inside the CDS columns, which makes _computeCodonAnalysis(sub,...) return null for that gene, and _computeAnnotatedCodonAnalysis drops it (script.js:5123 'continue') but still returns an object with genes:0. With Frame = Auto (default) the branch at 9452 fires: state._codonFrames is set to that empty gene result and the function returns at 9466, so the multi-frame analysis at 9470 is never computed. Body gets class 'codon-mode' but no codons, stops or translation rows are produced anywhere, and the toast at 9464 reads 'Codon analysis: 0 CDS from the annotation track, each in its own frame and strand' - zero CDS yet claiming each is translated. The user sees an empty Codon view despite a clean nucleotide alignment, with no fallback and no hint to use Pos 1/2/3.

title: MACSE codon-summary counts MACSE's terminal frameshift padding as a real frameshift (while the internal-stop count next to it correctly exempts the sequence end)
quote: for (let i = 0; i + 3 <= r.seq.length; i += 3) if (r.seq.slice(i, i + 3).includes('!')) n++;
scenario: Load a gene CDS in row 1 and a sample row that covers only part of the gene and is cropped so its length is not a multiple of 3; run 'Codon alignment -> MACSE'. macse-align.js pads the end of such a sequence to the next codon boundary with '!' markers (frameAminos: "if (out.length < nb) out.push(this.reliable ? '!' : '$');", read at macse-align.js:349). codonStats(nt, aa) walks the aligned row in fixed codon steps (line 51) and counts that final pad codon, so the summary returned to the page reports the row as having frameshifts when it is only truncated at the end. The internal-stop statistic computed just below in the same function explicitly exempts the sequence end (line 55 strips trailing [-!]+$, line 56 drops one final stop), showing that terminal '!' padding exists and is meant to be exempted for stops but is not for frameshifts.

quote: unmapped and QC-failed reads and bases below quality 13 are not counted. Indels are called as whole
scenario: Open a CRAM of the loaded gene and click Sample → row: cramToSamText emits every CRAM record with QUAL '*' instead of the real qualities, so SampleCall.baseQ (sample-call.js:24 "return qual === '*' ? 255") sends 255 for every base and line 53 counts any base whose "bq === 255". Thus the promised bases-below-quality-13 filter never rejects a CRAM base: noisy/low-quality bases participate in the consensus, the ≥20%-second-base IUPAC calls and the variant list (and downstream codon marks), unlike the same data opened as BAM or SAM.
title: Manual promises Q13 base filtering, but CRAM loads carry no qualities so every CRAM base is counted

scenario: Rename sample.bam (or sample.cram) to sample.sam and open it with the Open reads button: unlike drops, which go through _sniffReadsKind, this input calls handleBamFile with no event.readsKind, so handleBamFile takes ext='sam' from the name, reads the binary as text and parses it as SAM - no records and no @SQ survive, so the user gets the reference-mismatch message and no reads, although manual line 581 states "BAM and CRAM are recognised by their content, whatever the file is called". (A valid headerless SAM named .txt fails the same way, and the same accept attribute leaves .sam files out of the picker's default filter although the manual says a SAM file can be opened too.)
title: Open-reads dialog routes purely by file name: a BAM/CRAM renamed *.sam silently fails to load

quote: const { reads, refSeq, refStart, refEnd, columns, nTracks = 0 } = bamState;
scenario: Load a gene + a SAM mapped to it, view the reads, then edit a base of the reference sequence (or undo an edit) and stay in / return to Reads mode. bamState.refSeq is captured only at load time (it is never refreshed by edit/undo code; bamState is only rebuilt in handleBamFile, clearReadsData and parseAndRender), so renderReadsAlignment and _getReadCigarFeatures keep comparing the reads against the pre-edit string. The reference track shows the old base and the red mismatch marks are computed against it, so the mutation calls silently disagree with the alignment sequence the user just edited; there is no warning letting the reads go stale.
title: Reads view keeps the pre-edit reference: reference track and mismatch marks go stale after an edit or undo/redo

scenario: _getReadCigarFeatures records a D/N operation at its first reference position only, and this loop draws exactly one cellW-wide grey box per recorded position. A read with cigar '5M3D5M' therefore shows a 1 bp grey gap instead of 3 bp, and a read with a long N (intron) skip shows a single grey column at its start. For the user checking indels the drawn deletion length - the actual mutation - is wrong on screen; only the tooltip CIGAR reveals it.
title: Multi-base CIGAR deletions (and N skips) are drawn as a single one-column grey box
GenBank FEATURES (incl. CDS) are parsed and stored but never consumed by any part of the app - loading a GenBank gene has no effect on codon analysis or anywhere else
scenario: The user opens a GenBank file that has CDS features (the documented workflow: e.g. manual.html "GenBank with its CDS sets the reading frame", and the FEATURES table is claimed parsed in the release notes). parseGenBank (_parseGenbankRecord) does collect features into a _genbank {...} bag on the row, but grep over the whole repo shows no other line reads `._genbank` or `.location`/`.qualifiers` (they appear only at their creation sites inside the 4379-4534 parser). state.annot is set only from BED (parseBedFeatures -> state.annot = at line 8055), and the 'Genes' codon frame mode builds CDS exclusively from state.annot. So a GenBank-loaded CDS is silently ignored: no annotation track, no frame, no gene list; the documented way to give ViewAlign the gene's CDS simply does nothing.

title: Sample->row runs against the reference frozen at BAM-load; edits to the reference row afterwards are ignored (stale bases label the variants wrong)
scenario: bamState.refSeq is captured once when the reads are loaded (script.js:8635-8643) and never refreshed (greps show it is only assigned there and nulled on new-file load at 12357). Load gene + BAM, then let the user edit a base of the reference row (the row the sample row is placed against, refRow at 8902): change base 451 G->A to match the read evidence, then click Sample->row. SampleCall still counts hom/het and fills ref/alt in the variant list against the old G, so the message reports '451 A>G hom' although A is now row 1's base, and the '-'/IUPAC/'N' decisions are made against the obsolete sequence while the row is rendered against the edited one; if the edit removes/inserts a character in row 1 the position->column mapping (colOfPos, 8910) silently pairs every later base with the wrong reference position.

title: Clicking Sample->row a second time re-pads every row with the same insertion gap columns and appends a duplicate _sample row
scenario: Nothing in addSampleRowFromReads (8897-8944) guards against a sample row already added, and the button stays wired (8892). Trigger: reads carry a hom 3-base insertion, click Sample->row -> line 8920 splices three '-' gap columns into every row and a [ref]_sample row is added; click the button a second time -> the same three gap columns are spliced into every row AGAIN (now 6 columns of padding for the same insertion) and a second, identical [ref]_sample row is added, so every sequence and the gapless columns used by codon analysis are mangled. (I could not establish whether updateBamButtonVisibility re-shows/hides the button after the first click; the click handler itself has no re-entry guard.)

title: Per-gene aaSeq entries keep gene-local (sub-alignment) column numbers in e.src while e.cols are real alignment columns - a different meaning of src than the whole-alignment path uses
quote: const entries = r.aaSeq[i].map(e => ({ cols: e.cols.map(g).sort((a, b) => a - b), src: e.cols, codon: e.codon, aa: e.aa }));
scenario: With codon analysis 'Genes'/'Auto with CDS' the returned state._codonData is this byGene data: at line 5109 e.cols are mapped through g() to real alignment columns, but e.src is deliberately left as the gene-local columns (0..L-1; the polyA tail entry at 5117 does the same with src: tail). In the non-byGene path produced by _computeCodonAnalysis, e.src is a nucleotide/sequence-space index, and shared consumers such as _codonLanesForRange (line 5238: nuc: e.src?.[ci], paired with e.cols[ci]) assume src lines up with the row's own sequence coordinate under the full alignment; gene-local numbers only coincide when the gene starts at alignment column 0. For a gene elsewhere on the alignment those consumers sample the wrong nucleotide position of the row. I ran out of read budget before fully tracing the block renderer's use of the nuc field, so the consumer consequence is traced only up to _codonLanesForRange, hence confidence 2.

title: Copy/Download AA messages overstate the exported record count in Genes (byGene) frame mode
scenario: Load an alignment with a GenBank annotation containing two CDS features and enable Codon analysis; make one row cover only the first gene (e.g. a 'Sample -> row' sequence whose bases span gene 1 only, all gaps over gene 2). buildAATranslationFasta skips that row/gene record (line 14005 'if (!g.aa) continue;'), so the clipboard/file actually contains 5 records for a 3-row alignment (3 for gene 1 + 2 for gene 2), yet copyAATranslation (buildAATranslationFasta's caller at line 14047-14049) reports 'Copied 6 amino acid sequence(s) to clipboard!' and downloadAATranslation (line 14072) reports 'Saved 6 ... as ..._aa.fasta' — n x genes (3x2) instead of the real number of exported records (duplicate gene names merging in _aaByGene cause the same mismatch)

title: Auto-frame toast announces the frame number off-by-one (says "frame 0" for Pos 1 / "frame 2" for Pos 3)
scenario: Load a nucleotide alignment, turn on Codon analysis with Frame = Auto. bestFrame is a 0-based index (0..2) from _computeMultiFrameCodonAnalysis (script.js:5030), but the rest of the UI numbers frames 1-3: the select is labelled 'Pos 1/2/3' with values '0'/'1'/'2' and the legend rows print 'frame ' + (fr + 1) for fr=bestFrame (script.js:5350). When Auto picks the third position (bestFrame=2) the toast reads 'auto-selected frame 2', telling the user the analysis is in Pos 2 while it is actually in Pos 3; for Pos 1 it announces the non-existent 'frame 0'. It also appends '(ATG start)' even when the chosen frame has zero ATG starts (all scores 0 -> bestFrame falls to 0), so the message states a reason that does not exist.

A read aligned against the loaded gene whose CIGAR contains a deletion crossing the reference end (p + len > L). The whole D op is discarded: depth[p+i] is never incremented and the delEv Map never records key p:len, so the in-range part of the deletion produces no gap in the sample row and no del variant in the message - the row shows reference bases where every read is deleted - and the sample row's coverage picture silently differs from the Reads view.
title: Deletion events running past the reference end are dropped wholesale: no gap, no variant, no depth

scenario: Load a gene + SAM, view the reads, click 'Clear reads' (or load a new alignment while reads are loaded - parseAndRender resets bamState to an identical refEnd-less literal at script.js:12357). Those reset literals have no refEnd property, so when the user re-selects the 'Reads' radio, renderReadsAlignment gets refEnd = undefined, viewLen = NaN; the 'for (let p = refStart; p < refEnd; p++)' reference-track and ruler loops (9000/9033) never run and the SVG is sized from NaN. The Reads mode comes up completely blank instead of showing a proper empty panel, with no message.
title: bamState reset in clearReadsData (and on new-file load) omits refEnd, so re-entering Reads mode renders a blank view (viewLen = NaN)

scenario: A read with cigar '5M2I3M' carries the two inserted bases in SEQ. features.insertions stores only {refPos, len}; this render draws a single vertical tick at the boundary and the per-base letters (the cellW >= 7 branch) cover only the M/=/X positions in features.bases. The inserted nucleotides therefore never appear in the bar, the hover tooltip (name/pos/CIGAR/MAPQ only) or the click status line - the user checking an insertion cannot see what was inserted.
title: Inserted bases are never displayed - only a tick is drawn, the inserted sequence is dropped from the view, tooltip and status line

scenario: For a read with cigar e.g. '12S66M', the bar is drawn only from read.start (first aligned base) to read.end: _getReadCigarFeatures advances readPos for 'S' but records nothing for clipped bases, and renderReadsAlignment draws no clip cap/tail or clipped bases anywhere. The tooltip this line builds and the click status line report a CIGAR starting with 12S while the picture shows a read that appears to begin exactly at its mapped position, i.e. the clipping is stated in text but not shown.
title: Tooltip/status print a CIGAR that includes S soft-clips, but the picture shows no soft-clip marks at all
Sample row header claims 'called from N reads' including filtered-out reads
scenario: User loads a BAM/SAM containing duplicate (flag 0x400) or QC-fail (0x200) reads, or reads with mapq under the default 20, then clicks 'Sample -> row'. parseSAMToBuffer only skips 0x904 (line 8727) so those reads are still in bamState.reads, but SampleCall.call drops them (SKIP_FLAGS also includes 0x200/0x400, plus the mapq < minMapQ filter). The new row's fullHeader therefore states 'called from 200 reads' (line 8928) when e.g. only 150 reads actually contributed.

title: Ins variants report pos p+1 while the insertion sits between 1-based bases p and p+1 - one column right of the anchor used for every other variant type
quote: variants.push({ pos: p + 1, type: 'ins', ref: '-', alt: seq, zyg: hom ? 'hom' : 'het', depth: d, frac });
scenario: A hom 'GGT' insertion after 1-based base 122 arrives as insAfter key p=122 ('between reference positions p-1 and p', line 8, i.e. between 1-based 122 and 123). The pushed pos is 123, so the message (script.js:8938 prints 'ins GGT' next to the bare number) locates the insertion at/after base 123, one base right of where it was inserted, and inconsistent with the del/snv entries which name the first affected base (98, 123). A user checking the variants list against VCF-style reporting (anchor = preceding base, 122) or against the row display mis-places the insertion by one.

title: Sample-row header claims it is 'called from N reads' while the call skips flagged reads, so the stated depth of evidence is wrong
scenario: A BAM full of duplicate/secondary/QC-fail/supplementary alignments is loaded (the BAM branch pushes every record on the matched reference without a flag filter at script.js:8765-8781), while SampleCall (sample-call.js lines 40 and 18) skips 0x4/0x100/0x200/0x400/0x800 before counting. The header written at 8928 states 'called from 12,345 reads ...' even though only the non-flagged subset voted, so the evidence looks deeper than it is (the SAM branch already filters 0x904 at load, so the same file as text/SAM gives a different, smaller count than as BAM).
